To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the grid partition is a finite, discrete, and non-Euclidean geometric domain that is appropriate for the representation of fuzzy spatial objects; (b) fuzzy spatial objects can be represented by a finite number of crisp spatial objects, each of them being a crisp spatial object itself and having a crisp membership value; and (c) fuzzy spatial objects are represented by a finite set of crisp spatial objects.

(1) the fuzzy topological predicates of a spatial fuzzy object can be defined in terms of a crisp topological predicate and (2) the fuzzy spatial operations of a spatial fuzzy objects can be defined in the same manner as the fuzzy topological predicate.

the proposed model is able to handle both crisp and fuzzy spatial entities, and that its implementation is numerically robust and topologically consistent, and thus is able to provide correct answers to queries on fuzzy spatial entities.

the following questions: (1) How to model fuzzy geometric data? (2) How to implement the model? (3) How to manage the uncertainty of geometric data?
the design and implementation of finite-resolution crisp and fuzzy spatial entities and their geometric operations.

the following issues: (1) conceptual design of a fuzzy grid-based spatial data model; (2) implementation of the model in a spatial data management system; and (3) evaluation of the system in terms of its performance, its numerical robustness, and its topological consistency.

this paper provides a model of fuzzy spatial entities and operations which are based on a grid partition of the geometric space and are implementable with finite precision numbers.
this paper is a step towards a unified treatment of crisp and fuzzy spatial data.
this paper is a significant contribution to the area of spatial databases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an implementation model of spatial objects with fuzzy interiors and fuzzy boundaries which is based on the grid partition model and which is robust against finite precision arithmetic and numerical errors.

we have designed and implemented a model for finite resolution crisp and spatial objects that is able to deal with uncertainty of the geometric data and that is based on a finite, discretized geometric domain.
we have designed a finite, discrete model for fuzzy spatial objects and fuzzy geometric operations which are implemented in an object-oriented database management system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it provides a conceptual model and a prototype implementation of fuzzy spatial objects in a grid-partition-based framework which is not based on an infinite-precise arithmetic and is thus more suitable for implementation on a computer than existing approaches.
it is possible to develop a unified framework that allows for a crisp and a fuzzy treatment of both raster and vector data.
it provides a framework for a unified treatment of crisp and fuzzy spatial data.
